examples.text: Und sie ging gebückt, als trage sie eine schwere Last, […]
examples.ref: 1921, Elisabeth von Heyking, “Die Trommel”, in Weberin Schuld […] , Berlin: G. Grote'sche Verlagsbuchhandlung, page 18:
examples.english: And she walked bowed as if she carried a heavy load, […]
examples.translation: And she walked bowed as if she carried a heavy load, […]

examples.text: Seine Lider waren wie Blei so schwer, die Zunge gehorchte dem einfachen Gedanken nicht recht, als er aus Artigkeit mit der Engländerin zu plaudern versuchte; […].
examples.ref: 1924, Thomas Mann, Der Zauberberg [The Magic Mountain], volume 1, Berlin: S. Fischer, page 118; republished as Helen T. Lowe-Porter, transl., The Magic Mountain, 1927:
examples.english: His eyelids were heavy as lead; his tongue would not shape his simple thoughts when out of politeness he tried to talk to the Englishwoman.
examples.translation: His eyelids were heavy as lead; his tongue would not shape his simple thoughts when out of politeness he tried to talk to the Englishwoman.

examples.text: „Es ist überhaupt keine Zeit“, sagte Hans Castorp mit schwerer Zunge.
examples.ref: 1924, Thomas Mann, Der Zauberberg [The Magic Mountain], volume 1, Berlin: S. Fischer, page 32; republished as Helen T. Lowe-Porter, transl., The Magic Mountain, 1927:
examples.english: “You can't call it time,” quoth Hans Castorp thick-tongued.
examples.translation: “You can't call it time,” quoth Hans Castorp thick-tongued.

examples.text: [Director.] So könnt ihr euch vom Ziele nie verirren, / Sucht nur die Menschen zu verwirren, / Sie zu befriedigen ist schwer – –
examples.ref: 1808, Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, “Vorspiel auf dem Theater”, in Faust: Der Tragödie erster Teil [Faust, Part One]; republished as Bayard Taylor, transl., 1870:
examples.english: Thus shall you hit the mark of gain and glory / Seek to confound your auditory! / To satisfy them is a task.—
examples.translation: Thus shall you hit the mark of gain and glory / Seek to confound your auditory! / To satisfy them is a task.—

examples.text: Sein Alter wäre schwer zu schätzen gewesen, zwischen dreißig und vierzig mußte es wohl liegen […].
examples.ref: 1924, Thomas Mann, Der Zauberberg [The Magic Mountain], volume 1, Berlin: S. Fischer, page 96; republished as Helen T. Lowe-Porter, transl., The Magic Mountain, 1927:
examples.english: His age would have been hard to say, probably between thirty and forty […]
examples.translation: His age would have been hard to say, probably between thirty and forty […]

examples.text: Ich habe gefehlt, und es ist gar nicht mit Worten zu sagen, wie schwer ich gefehlt habe!
examples.ref: 1913 [1878], chapter 4, in Hermann Röhl, transl., Anna Karenina, translation of Анна Каренина (Anna Karenina) by Leo Tolstoy, part 1:
examples.english: I am to blame, no words can express how much I am to blame!
examples.translation: I am to blame, no words can express how much I am to blame!

raw.etymology_text: From Middle High German swær, from Old High German swār, from Proto-West Germanic *swār, from Proto-Germanic *swēraz, from Proto-Indo-European *swer- (“heavy, grave, serious”).
